situation: xAI needs a training cluster of 100,000 GPUs and needs it now. Datacentre builders quote 18 to 24 months. Any site with adequate grid power has a multi-year interconnection queue in front of it.
what_he_actually_did: Rejected the quoted timeline. Took a shuttered Electrolux appliance factory in Memphis — closed since 2020, 785,000 sq ft — instead of building new. The local grid connection was about 8MW against a need near 130MW, so rather than wait for the interconnect he ran the site on temporary natural-gas turbines and Tesla Megapacks. 100,000 H100s live in 122 days; doubled to 200,000 in a further 92.
outcome_detail: Operational July 2024. Nvidia's CEO called the build 'superhuman'. The approach has since drawn sustained local opposition over the gas turbines' air quality impact in south Memphis — a cost borne by people who were not party to the decision.

expect.notes: A generalisation check on the 2018 tent rules, six years later and three orders of magnitude larger. Same shape: delete the requirement that the building be new, delete the requirement that power come from the grid, accept something temporary and ugly, move. If the stopgap correction and the unowned-requirement rule were fitted to 2018 rather than real, this is where that shows.

decision.decision: Stand up 100,000 GPUs for training as fast as physically possible

requirements.text: The facility must be a purpose-built datacentre
The site must be connected to adequate utility grid power before operating
The cluster must train a frontier model this year

steps.name: Run on temporary gas turbines and Megapacks until the interconnect lands
Wait for the utility interconnection queue
Build a new facility to spec

components.name: Time to first training run, against the industry quote
